flashcards.q: Azure OpenAI deployment types and processing scopes?
flashcards.a: GlobalStandard ($/token, ANY region, best quotas/newest models); DataZone* (US|EU|APAC bounds); Standard (single-region); *ProvisionedManaged (reserved PTUs); GlobalBatch (~50% off, 24 h window); DeveloperTier (fine-tune eval, ~24 h life, no SLA).
Stored data always stays in designated geography; INFERENCE PROCESSING follows deployment scope - Global may process anywhere. Conflating these is how audit findings happen.
Quota = policy TPM ceiling per subscription/region/type; capacity = physical compute HELD at deployment time. Owning quota does not guarantee capacity - check capacities API before committing dates.
RPM x avg input tokens x output-to-input ratio (output consumes more capacity), reduced by prompt-cache hit rate; normalize to TPM-equivalent, divide by model's input-TPM-per-PTU.
Backoff WITH jitter; separate deployments per criticality so batch can't starve interactive; async work to Batch API (~50% off); client concurrency caps; cache-first prompt structure.
Parallel BM25 + HNSW vector queries fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion: score(d) = SUM 1/(k+rank), k~60; consensus beats either signal alone.

flashcards.q: Semantic ranker function and score scale?
flashcards.a: L2 cross-encoder (Bing-derived) rescoring fused top-N over ~2048-token summaries (was 256 before Nov 2024); rerankerScore 4->0; paid per query beyond monthly free allowance.
Filter permissions INSIDE the query before top-k truncation; post-filtering displaces results and risks leaks. Never rely on the LLM respecting permissions it can see violated.

flashcards.q: Foundry Agent Service Basic vs Standard setup?
flashcards.a: Basic: state in Microsoft-managed storage. Standard: capability hosts bind YOUR resources - Cosmos DB threads, AI Search vectors, Blob files; the compliance answer for regulated transcripts.
~128 tools per agent, ~100k messages/thread, ~512 MB max file, ~10k files per context, ~1000 valid revisions; service is GA.
One URL fronts named deployments; shift traffic % gradually; mirror mode shadows traffic without affecting responses (doubles compute); safe-pull auto-rollbacks on errors.

flashcards.q: When is fine-tuning justified over better RAG?
flashcards.a: Format/style compression, token-cost reduction replacing few-shot blocks, distilling frontier quality into small models. NOT for injecting facts - knowledge belongs retrievable-side (fresh, citable, updatable).
Below ~100k-1M chunks with relational metadata needs: pgvector on PostgreSQL Flexible. Above that or needing faceting/multi-language/security-trim/semantic-ranker lift: AI Search.
As annotated empty/refused outputs carrying filter-result metadata, not exceptions; apps must distinguish filtered-empty from genuine-empty or ship silent-failure UX.
